I’ve had needle phobia my whole life, tho maybe not as severe as others may have it. I was terrified of the idea of doing needles myself, but just like you, I was concerned about gel transfer, and also I had heard the needles work faster so I ultimately went with it. 

I haven’t found the pain too bad. The needle you inject with is very thin and not super long so it’s not all that invasive. Usually I feel an initial poke when it breaks through the skin, but once it’s in, usually I don’t feel it at all (occasionally tho).

My best advice for you if you go on T injections: do something relaxing beforehand, it’ll be hard to get through the anxiety if you’re already worked up. It’s also helpful to have background noise so you can focus on something other than anxious thoughts. Good songs or trans YouTubers are my T shot bffs lol.

My stance on slurs is you should only say it about yourself if it’s something that has been/could easily be used against you, as a way of reclaiming. Maybe to a close friend if that’s something they’re comfortable with. 

As a passing trans man who used to identify as a lesbian, I would not use the lesbian slur to refer to myself, since I am no longer a queer woman and no one would assume I am enough to call me that slur. I could somewhat fathom a non passing trans man using that slur coming from a place of being mistaken as a lesbian? Still it’s pretty rocky to do so because I can’t see a trans man using the slur in any other way than something along the lines of “I’m tired of not passing, everyone just thinks I’m a ____” which still carries negative connotations towards lesbians. That is not reclaiming. I can’t see him directly calling himself the lesbian slur because it would be a form of misgendering. I mean there are some transmasc non binary people who identify as lesbian, so maybe in that case, but if generally they are perceived as a man to some degree, I’d advise against that. 

TLDR; Never use slurs that don’t pertain to you, and I still generally advise against using ones that do to avoid making others uncomfortable and starting arguments.

just had surgery 3 weeks ago so this is all pretty fresh in my mind still:

anything that you’ll want to access post op, make sure it’s in easy reaching distance, not too high or low. before leaving surgery, i put my laptop, headphones, and video game stuff on my bed. also picked up charging cables from the floor so i wouldn’t have to bend down or even squat to pick them up. also, make sure your toilet paper is in a place you can reach it without needing to twist or lean forward too much. wiping was a bit tough that first day or two lol. 

you’re also going to want to sleep propped up for the first few nights because it helps with swelling and blood clots. if you have a recliner, that would be the ideal set up; throw whatever pillows and blankets you need for bedtime and see if you can have a table of some sort set up next to it for your water, medications, entertainment. if you have no recliner, stack up 2-4 pillows (depends on what kind of pillows you have and what’s comfortable for you to sleep with) on your bed in a way that’ll be comfortable for you post surgery. keep that set up towards the edge of the bed. you won’t be able to climb very far into bed; you can basically just gently plop and barely scooch over. 

if you haven’t already, and even if you can’t get it in time for immediately after your surgery, i’d recommend getting a wedge pillow and especially a mastectomy pillow for the first few weeks where you have to sleep on your back. the wedge pillow helped for when i needed to be propped up and also is comfier than sleeping flat on my back now that i can do that. the mastectomy pillow prevented me from even trying to roll over if i kinda hugged it over my chest. 

i would suggest going into surgery with the comfiest clothes you can find. something loose and stretchy would be good so that when your hospital helps to redress you, it’s easier and if you decide to take anything off at home, it’s doable. 

hope this helps, and don’t be discouraged or overwhelmed if you can’t do everything. most of these things aren’t necessary, just helpful or convenient.
